cur-fossil-seymour-island.dateNote: In December 1892 the whaling captain Carl Anton Larsen landed here and collected fossil shells and wood — the first fossils from Antarctica. The rocks are about 70–34 million years old (Late Cretaceous to Eocene).
cur-fossil-seymour-island.summary: The island where the first fossils from Antarctica were collected.

cur-fossil-james-ross-island.dateNote: In January 1986 Eduardo Olivero and Roberto Scasso found an armoured dinosaur here, later named Antarctopelta: the first dinosaur found in Antarctica. The rock is about 74–70 million years old (Late Cretaceous). Wikidata pins the island; the bones came from near Santa Marta Cove.
cur-fossil-james-ross-island.summary: Where the first dinosaur bones in Antarctica were found.
